compensating.why: hop 1 adds the Unix directory type to the mode of a directory entry
hop 3 keeps only the permission bits of the mode
hop 4 marks the mode of a directory entry with 0x10

ownership_reason: Only the gold builds the external attribute word of the entry: it places the Unix mode in the upper two bytes, sets the lower-byte marks and sets the word on the entry. Hops 1-4 pass the entry and the mode on unchanged and set nothing themselves; the facade adds only the platform. The lower bytes of the variant's word hold only the mark derived from the owner-write bit, so no mode a caller passes makes a directory entry carry the directory attribute 0x10; once the gold has set the word without it, it can appear only if a caller rewrites the attributes the gold set or replaces the gold. The gold promises the external attributes of the entry from its Unix mode; the facade documents them as those understood by Info-Zip's unzip, in which a directory carries the directory attribute, and the variant leaves it out for the directory entry foo/. The convention that a directory entry's Unix attributes record that it is a directory is pinned outside the gold: AsiExtraField.getMode(int) stores the directory type DIR_FLAG with the mode of a directory entry, ZipArchiveEntry.isDirectory() makes a name ending in '/' a directory and ZipArchiveEntry.getUnixMode() reads the mode back from the upper two bytes; AsiExtraFieldTest::testModes and ::testReparse (a directory's mode carries the directory type) and ZipTestCase::testExplicitDirectoryEntry (the entry foo/ is a directory) pass.
